MIDWEST SAFETY: Uncover. Inform. Empower.

Please consider JOINING for $1 a month. It *really* helps us do original reporting like this. 

MERCH! Midwest-Safety.com

CONTACT US:
Complaints? Video submissions? Tips? Sponsorships? Collabs? Business inquires? 
Email our board at mn.safety.alerts@gmail.com. 

BE NICE:
The individuals presented in these videos may be suffering from the effects of alcohol, drug abuse, a mental health disorder or simply having a bad day. The videos should NOT be presumed to be representative of their general behavior. Everyone deserves to be treated with respect. 

RIGHT TO BE FORGOTTEN:
Midwest Safety practices the "Right to be Forgotten." If you were the suspect in a lower-level offense, you may email our board to request removal. 
Email: mn.safety.alerts@gmail.com

While 22-year-old Ian Kuypers was cited for driving the wrong way on a one-way street and resisting, obstructing, he held true to his statement about appealing the resisting, obstructing charge. On July 16, 2024, a jury acquitted Ian of that charge. Now, Ian and his attorneys have filed a multi-count federal civil rights lawsuit against the City of Superior, Wisconsin, and multiple Superior Police Department officers involved in the incident. The lawsuit claims excessive force and failure to intervene against the officers and indemnification, which is where one party compensates another for losses against the City of Superior. Ian has since said that he received a diagnosis of post-traumatic stress disorder related to the incident, for which he is receiving ongoing therapy and has been prescribed medication. He has also since moved to Denver, Colorado, after no longer feeling safe living in the Superior area. He also claims to feel extreme distress while driving, causing him to no longer work for DoorDash. In addition, he also lost his job in Denver due to having to travel back to Wisconsin for his criminal trial. Police Chief Paul Wintershite has since stated that the use of a taser during the traffic stop was due to Ian's continued resistance, claiming that the taser was deployed to prevent the situation from escalating. While it's unclear how the lawsuit has progressed, let us know in the comments what you think about it. And always remember, the body camera doesn't always show the full story.
